title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE HONORABLE TREATMENT OF FORMER PRESIDENTS
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE HONORABLE TREATMENT OF FORMER PRESIDENTS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended 2010.2.4>

Article 2 (Definitions of Terms)
(1) "Annual remuneration of the President at the time of payment" in Articles 4 (2) and 5 (1) of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means an amount equivalent to 8.85 times the monthly amount of the President's annual salary for the month in which the pension payment date falls. <Amended 1988.3.18, 2000.1.8, 2010.2.4>
(2) "Surviving children aged 30 or older who are unable to earn a livelihood" in Article 5 (2) of the Act means persons who, taking into account the income, assets, dependents, etc. of the surviving children and their families, are considered under generally accepted social standards to have difficulty maintaining the dignity befitting surviving children of a former President. <Added 1981.4.8>

Article 3 (Pension Certificates)
(1) A person who becomes entitled to a survivor pension shall apply to the Minister of the Interior and Safety for issuance of a pension certificate, accompanied by the relevant documents necessary to substantiate entitlement to the survivor pension. <Amended 2000.1.8, 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall issue pension certificates in the attached Form to former Presidents and persons entitled to survivor pensions. In such cases, where necessary for issuing a pension certificate, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may request the relevant person entitled to a pension to submit supporting documents, etc. <Amended 2000.1.8, 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
(3) Where there are multiple persons entitled to a survivor pension under Article 5 (2) of the Act, a single pension certificate listing the names, etc. of all persons entitled to the survivor pension may be issued.

Article 4 (Period of Pension Payments)
A pension shall be paid from the month following the month in which the grounds for payment arise through the month in which those grounds cease to exist.

Article 5 (Pension Payment Date)
A pension shall be paid in 12 monthly installments, on the 20th day of each month.

Article 6 (Suspension of Pension Payments)
Where grounds for suspending pension payments arise pursuant to Article 7 of the Act, payments shall be suspended from the month following the month in which those grounds arise through the month in which those grounds cease to exist.

Article 6-2 (Support for Commemorative Projects)
(1) The commemorative projects supported pursuant to Article 5-2 of the Act shall be as follows: <Added 2011.9.6, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
1. Projects to construct memorial halls and memorial libraries for former Presidents;
2. Projects to collect and organize historical materials related to former Presidents, including records and personal effects;
3. Projects to research and compile the achievements, etc. of former Presidents;
4. Projects for the exhibition and inspection of historical materials and other materials, etc. specified in subparagraphs 2 and 3;
5. Projects to hold academic seminars or operate lecture courses, etc. related to former Presidents;
6. External cooperation projects, including holding international academic conferences related to former Presidents;
7. Other projects equivalent to those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 6 that are determined by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
(2) The support for commemorative projects under paragraph (1) shall be as follows: <Amended 2011.9.6>
1. Lending exhibits, such as documents and drawings;
2. Subsidizing part of the project expenses;
3. Other support deemed necessary for implementing projects.
(3) The recipients and scale of support under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be determined following deliberation by the State Council. <Amended 2011.9.6>

Article 6-3 (Support for Grave Management)
(1) Personnel required for grave management for whom support may be provided pursuant to Article 5-3 of the Act shall be grave security personnel and management personnel. In such cases, support may be paid in the form of costs of deploying such personnel, taking into consideration the efficiency of grave management, etc.
(2) Costs required for grave management for which support may be provided pursuant to Article 5-3 of the Act shall be management costs, such as maintenance of grave facilities.
(3) Costs under the latter part of paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be paid to the bereaved family managing the grave; where an organization manages the grave with the consent of the bereaved family, those costs may be paid to that organization: Provided, That where there is no bereaved family or organization managing the grave, those costs may be paid to a person whom the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems it necessary to support for grave management.
(4) A person who intends to receive support under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall submit to the Minister of the Interior and Safety application documents containing necessary matters, such as the personnel and costs required for grave management.
(5) The specific persons eligible for support, the scale and methods of support, etc. under paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be separately determined by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 7 (Appointment of Secretaries, etc.)
(1) A secretary to a former President shall be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the Minister of the Interior and Safety submitted through the Prime Minister, and a driver shall be appointed by the Minister of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
(2) A secretary to the spouse of a deceased former President shall be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the Minister of the Interior and Safety submitted through the Prime Minister, and a driver shall be appointed by the Minister of the Interior and Safety; the secretary shall be a special-service public official belonging to the Senior Civil Service, and the driver shall be a special-service public official. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>
(3) Deleted <2011.9.6>

Article 7-2 (Medical Treatment Free of Charge)
Medical treatment of former Presidents and their spouses at national or public hospitals (including Seoul National University Hospital under the Seoul National University Hospital Establishment Act, Seoul National University Dental Hospital under the Seoul National University Dental Hospital Establishment Act, national university hospitals under the Act on Establishment of National University Hospitals, and national university dental hospitals under the Act on Establishment of National University Dental Hospitals) shall be free of charge, and the State shall bear the costs incurred for their medical treatment at private medical institutions. <Amended 1988.3.18, 2000.1.8, 2010.2.4, 2011.9.6>

Article 7-3 (Provision of Offices, etc.)
The details of support under Article 6 (4) 2 of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended 2010.2.4>
1. Provision of offices and vehicles and payment of other operating expenses;
2. Payment of travel expenses, etc. for official travel.

Article 8 (Budgetary Measures)
The budget for pensions for former Presidents and their bereaved families shall be included in the general account of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety. <Amended 1981.4.8, 2000.1.8, 2008.2.29, 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26>

Article 9 (Processing of Sensitive Information and Unique Identifying Information)
The Minister of the Interior and Safety may process materials containing information concerning health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act, information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act, or resident registration numbers, passport numbers, or alien registration numbers under subparagraph 1, 2, or 4 of Article 19 of that Decree where it is unavoidable for the performance of the following affairs:
1. Affairs concerning payment of pensions under Articles 4 and 5 of the Act;
2. Affairs concerning support for grave management under Article 5-3 of the Act;
3. Affairs concerning support, such as transportation, communications, and provision of offices, and affairs concerning medical treatment for the person concerned and his or her family under Article 6 (4) 2 and 3 of the Act;
4. Affairs concerning suspension of and exclusion from honorable treatment of former Presidents under Article 7 (2) of the Act.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 3753, January 29, 1969>

(1) (Enforcement Date) This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

(2) (Transitional Measures) Pension payments first made under this Decree shall, notwithstanding Article 4, commence with the amount payable for the month in which the Act enters into force.

ADDENDA (Public Officials Remuneration Regulations) <Presidential Decree No. 7938, December 31, 1975>

(1) (Enforcement Date) This Decree shall enter into force on January 1, 1976.

(2) through (6) Omitted.

(7) (Alignment of Related Statutes and Regulations) Following the amendment of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations, related statutes and regulations shall be amended as follows:

1. In Article 7 (3) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents, "Article 19 of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations" shall be replaced by "Article 16 of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations".

2. Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 10282, April 8, 1981>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 12417, March 18, 1988>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 16688, January 8, 2000>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That the amended provisions of Article 2 (1) shall apply from January 1, 2000.

ADDENDA (Regulations on the Organization of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and Its Affiliated Agencies) <Presidential Decree No. 20741, February 29, 2008>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. <Proviso Omitted.>

Articles 2 through 5 Omitted.

Article 6 (Amendments to Other Statutes and Regulations)
(1) through (65) Omitted.

(66) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents shall be amended in part as follows:

In Article 3 (1), the former and latter parts of Article 3 (2), and Article 7, "Minister of the Interior" shall each be replaced by "Minister of the Interior and Safety".

In Article 8, "Ministry of the Interior" shall be replaced by "Ministry of the Interior and Safety".

On pages 3 and 4 of the attached Form, "Minister of the Interior" shall each be replaced by "Minister of the Interior and Safety".

(67) through (105) Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 22011, February 4, 2010>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Special Cases)
Notwithstanding the amended provisions of the main clause of Article 7 (3), the terms of appointment of the secretary and driver serving the spouse of a former President who died before this Decree enters into force shall each be three years from the date of appointment.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 23117, September 6, 2011>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA (Organization of the Ministry of Security and Public Administration and Its Affiliated Agencies) <Presidential Decree No. 24425, March 23, 2013>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That, among the Presidential Decrees amended pursuant to Article 6 of the Addenda, the portions amending Presidential Decrees that have been promulgated before this Decree enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall each enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant Presidential Decree.

Articles 2 through 5 Omitted.

Article 6 (Amendment of Other Statutes and Regulations)
(1) through (84) Omitted.

(85) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents is partially amended as follows:

In Article 3 (1), the former and latter parts of paragraph (2) of that Article, Article 6-2 (1) 7, and Article 7 (1) and (2), each occurrence of "Minister of the Interior and Safety" shall be replaced by "Minister of Security and Public Administration".

In Article 8, "Ministry of the Interior and Safety" shall be replaced by "Ministry of Security and Public Administration".

In the attached Form, each occurrence of "Minister of the Interior and Safety" shall be replaced by "Minister of Security and Public Administration".

(86) through (129) Omitted.

ADDENDA (Organization of the Ministry of the Interior and Its Affiliated Agencies) <Presidential Decree No. 25751, November 19, 2014>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That, among the Presidential Decrees amended pursuant to Article 5 of the Addenda, the portions amending Presidential Decrees that have been promulgated before this Decree enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall each enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant Presidential Decree.

Articles 2 through 4 Omitted.

Article 5 (Amendment of Other Statutes and Regulations)
(1) through (196) Omitted.

(197) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents is partially amended as follows:

In Article 3 (1), the former and latter parts of paragraph (2) of that Article, Article 6-2 (1) 7, and Article 7 (1) and (2), each occurrence of "Minister of Security and Public Administration" shall be replaced by "Minister of the Interior".

In Article 8, "Ministry of Security and Public Administration" shall be replaced by "Ministry of the Interior".

On pages 3 and 4 of the attached Form, each occurrence of "Minister of Security and Public Administration" shall be replaced by "Minister of the Interior".

(198) through (418) Omitted.

ADDENDA (Decree on Partial Amendment of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Excavation of Remains of Soldiers Killed in the Korean War and Other Presidential Decrees to Minimize Collection of Resident Registration Numbers) <Presidential Decree No. 26774, December 30, 2015>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. <Proviso Omitted.>

ADDENDA (Organization of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and Its Affiliated Agencies) <Presidential Decree No. 28211, July 26, 2017>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That, among the Presidential Decrees amended pursuant to Article 8 of the Addenda, the portions amending Presidential Decrees that have been promulgated before this Decree enters into force but whose enforcement dates have not yet arrived shall each enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant Presidential Decree.

Articles 2 through 7 Omitted.

Article 8 (Amendment of Other Statutes and Regulations)
(1) through (153) Omitted.

(154) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents is partially amended as follows:

In Article 3 (1), the former and latter parts of paragraph (2) of that Article, Article 6-2 (1) 7, and Article 7 (1) and (2), each occurrence of "Minister of the Interior" shall be replaced by "Minister of the Interior and Safety".

In Article 8, "general account of the Ministry of the Interior" shall be replaced by "general account of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety".

On page 3 of the attached Form, in the portion of subparagraph 2 on page 4 of that Form other than its items, and in subparagraph 3 on the same page, each occurrence of "Minister of the Interior" shall be replaced by "Minister of the Interior and Safety".

(155) through (388) Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 28300, September 19, 2017>

This Decree shall enter into force on September 22, 2017.

ADDENDA (Presidential Decree on Partial Amendment of 473 Statutes and Regulations to Revise Difficult Legal Terminology) <Presidential Decree No. 31380, January 5, 2021>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation. <Proviso Omitted.>
